body: Ping, any idea what might be causing this? (still happens in the latest version)
As workaround you can `[name]` instead of `[chunkhash]` for development and use `[chunkhash]` only in production..
For some reason hot builds don't have this problem so I'm not seriously affected (but I still keep a non-hot watcher running for non-developers).

It appears that even when using `[id]` (should be equivalent to `[name]` I assume) only the initial build works, subsequent builds don't break, but they don't actually seem to include any changes either.

Still having the same issues, initial build is OK, incremental builds doesn't actually reflect the changes.

Initial build says:

```
...
static/0.js  1340118       0  [emitted]
static/index.js   383558       1  [emitted]   entry
```

Incremental build says:

```
static/2.js  1340118       2  [emitted]
```

`static/2.js` is obviously new and not `static/0.js` but it's never actually used (`static/index.js` isn't updated either). It seems the names are getting mixed up?

Perhaps it's documented somewhere, but this was caused by...

```
new webpack.optimize.OccurrenceOrderPlugin()
```

...being used with incremental builds which kind of makes sense (perhaps throw an error if it's not allowed?).

Weird... I've no idea what could be the error, if it's not the bug i've fixed (Are you using 1.4.9?). You could prepare a test case for this so I could take a closer look.

`OccurrenceOrderPlugin` is allowed.

@sokra Was using `1.4.7` I think, but just updated and same issue is present with `1.4.9`.

Doubt it has any relevance, but:
When I'm running without `OccurrenceOrderPlugin` I get the following order:

```
       static/index.js   383361       0  [emitted]  entry
      static/chunk.1.js  1340332       1  [emitted]
```

But when using `OccurrenceOrderPlugin` I get the following order:

```
      static/chunk.0.js  1339558       0  [emitted]
       static/index.js   383384       1  [emitted]  entry
```

Incremental builds then adds and updates `chunk.2.js` instead of `chunk.0.js` as I mention in the post above. I only have a single split-point.
I relied on the new watching plugin for quite a while which actually solved it, and now that it is standard I'm no longer seeing this problem. Closing... but it seems fishy...

@syranide I'm facing this same issue with my webpack configuration and `OccurrenceOrderPlugin` which I need in order to keep the `chunkhash`es consistent across webpack builds. What was your final solution for this?

@tazsingh I simply stopped using that plugin in watcher builds and as I mention above, since the new watcher plugin became standard I haven't seen this issue again (still not using OccurenceOrderPlugin with watcher though)... but yeah, the underlying problem is most likely still there.

Ok thanks @syranide. Unfortunately that solution does not work for me.

I have to use the `OccurrenceOrderPlugin` as without it the order of modules changes in the chunks for every build and therefore affects the `chunkhash`es across deploys.

I also note that for the chunk with id of `0`, the chunkhash is `undefined`, and those modules seem to have issues loading both in development and production.

Would you mind re-opening this issue since the problem is still there? Not sure if you can somehow transfer the issue over to me but I'm also happy to open another one if that's easiest.
@tazsingh Use OccurrenceOrderPlugin when deploying, don't use it when in dev-watcher mode, that's what I do (not an actual fix, just saying :)).

@syranide Aye I tried that but the `chunkhash`es are still different between builds which is the issue I need `OccurrenceOrderPlugin` for :( Also doesn't fix that modules for id `0` chunkhash `undefined` aren't loading in production and only load the 1st time in development.

Looking at the module itself, it's pretty small and I'm going to try to debug myself when I have a moment. Unless someone gets to it before I do ;)
